verses.text: EikhahPoem 1 beginning with Jerusalem: How is it conceivableThat the city once teeming with peopleNow sits isolated Having become like a widow.That she who was once the great one among the nations,The noble among the provinces,Has become a vassal laborer.

She weeps bitterly in the night —Her tears lie undried on her cheeks,For there are none to console herAmong all her lovers.On the contrary:All her friends have betrayed her;They have become her enemies.

Judea has been exiledFor she was unable to bear the poverty and excessive labourWrought by her vassal status.But when she attempted to settle among the nations,She found no rest.All who once trailed herHave now overtaken herAs she navigates between the constraints imposed on her.

The roads of Zion are mournful,For they are now bereft of festival pilgrims.All her gates are desolate,For her elders and scholars are no longer.Her priests groan rather than chant the service;Her young women grieve rather than rejoice;Her lot is bitter rather than sweet.

Her oppressors have taken the lead;Her enemies have enjoyed serenity;For YHWH had her grieveFor her excessive transgressions.Her (Judea’s) beautiful infants were marched into captivity,Before the oppressorTo be exploited and to advance his interests.

Likewise,All dignity departed the community of Zion.Her talented officials have become redundant —Like harts that find no pasture;They too now marchDepleted of strengthBefore those who once trailed her.

Jerusalem now remembers —In her days of poverty and downtroddenness —All that she treasured in bygone times.How when her people fell into the hand of the oppressorNo one came to her assistance;How her oppressors had looked onAnd mocked the suspension of her grandeur.
Jerusalem sinned grievously,She therefore became contemptible;All who once honoured her now belittle her,For she has been laid bare;She too groanedAs she came undone.

Her filth was paraded on her skirt hems;For she gave no thought to her future.Is it thus surprisingThat she has sunk to such depthsWith none to comfort her!?Look, O YHWH at my affliction,Do You not seeThat the enemy has become great!
Look how the oppressor has stretched his handOver all Zion’s treasures;She has even witnessed nationsInvade her sanctuary,Those whom You forbadeTo enter Your congregation.
Look how all Judea’s people groanAs they search for bread;How they must trade their treasures for foodTo revive their lives.Look, O YHWH, and considerHow belittled I have become.

May no such fate befall you all passersby.Consider and look:Is there any agony as intense as my agony —That was deliberately delivered to me!?Like the grief YHWH had me sufferOn the day His wrath flared!?
For, from on highHe sent fire into my bonesAnd hammered them.He spread a net for my feet to ensnare me;He made me come undone.He made me devastated;Sickened all day long.

The yoke of my transgressionsLay exposed in His handThere, they grew, entangled,Gradually climbing over my neck,And sapping my strength.Adonai — my master — has delivered me into handsFrom which I cannot possibly rise again.
Adonai trampled all my strongmenIn my midst.He proclaimed a festivalFor shattering my young men.Adonai has trodden as in a winepressThe Judean community’s young women.

For these things I weep;Tears relentlessly tumble from my eyes;For a comforter who might revive my spiritHas distanced themself from me.My children have become desolate,For the enemy has overpowered us.

Zion stretches her hands to her contemporaries,But none provide her with comfort.YHWH had providentially commanded from time immemorial that Jacob — the JudeansBe surrounded by his oppressors.Jerusalem has become contemptible among them.
YHWH is in the right,For I have rebelled against His word.Listen here — take heed — all you peoples:Look at my agony —At my young women and young menWho have gone into captivity.

At how I called to my lovers,Yet they deceived me;At how my priests and scholarly elders perished in the cityWhile searching for food to revive their lives.Is this not unprecedented and providential?Beware! That same providence shall come back to bite you!

Look, O YHWH,For I am distressed;My gut is wrenched.I have experienced a change of heart,For I accept that I have been very rebellious.Look! Outdoors, the sword brings bereavement,Indoors, it is like death.

Look at how they heard that I was groaning,Yet no one comforted me.On the contrary —All my enemies heard of my trouble and delightedBecause, to their minds, You had done it.Please, restore Your providence:Bring on the day You announced,When they will be as I am now.

Let all their evil doings come before You,And deliberately deliver punishment to themLike You deliberately delivered punishment to meFor of all my transgressions.For they have made me suffer bitterly:My groans are many and my heart is faint.

POEM II: The ConvergenceHow is it conceivableThat Adonai in His angerShrouded the community of Zion in storm clouds!?He threw down from heaven to earthThe glory of Israel;He did not remember His footstool — the epicentre of His worldly manifestationOn the day of His anger.
Adonai devoured without mercyAll the fine abodes of Jacob;In His wrath he demolishedThe strongholds of the Judean community —Toppling them to the ground.He desecrated a kingdom and its officials.
He cut down in raging angerThe entire headship of Israel;He withdrew His protective right handIn the face of the enemy;His rage blazed in Jacob like a flaming fire,Consuming all around.

His protective right hand was not merely paralyzed — it persecuted:He bent His bow like an enemy,His right hand set about it like a foe.He killed all those desirable to behold.In the tent of the community of ZionHis fury was vented like fire.
Adonai became like an enemy:He devoured Israel,He devoured all its palaces,And destroyed all its strongholds.He advanced grief and mourningWithin the Judean community.

He laid bare His abode as though it were a garden;He destroyed His place of commune.He banished YHWH from Zion’s memory;He abolished its Shabbat and festival services.In his ferocious angerHe spurned king and priest.

Adonai distanced Himself from His altar,He Rejected His sanctuary.He delivered the walls of Zion’s palacesInto the hand of the enemy.They raised a clamour in the house of YHWHAs though it was a festival day.

YHWH schemed to destroyThe protective wall of the community of Zion;He planned meticulouslyAs though stretching a plumb line;Then, He did not withhold His hand from devouring them.He cast her protective walls and ramparts into mourning,As they were made barren together.

Her gates sunk into the ground,He decommissioned and broke her locks.He let her leadership collapse:Now her king and prince are exiled among the nations;She has no religious counsel;Even Her prophets cannot encounter a vision from YHWH.

Now the scholarly elders of the community of ZionSit on the ground;They are silent.They have heaved dirt onto their heads,They have girded themselves with sackcloth.Now the once proud young women of JerusalemBow their heads to the ground in shame.

My eyes are spent with weeping,My gut is wrenched,My liver is spilled on the ground,Because of the destruction of my community;At the writhing of its infants and suckling babesIn the main roads of the city.
They cry out to their mothers:"Where is bread and wine?"As they writhe like the dismemberedIn the main roads of the city;As their souls ebb awayIn their mothers’ embrace.

Who could testify to your torment,What could be likened to your lot,O community of Jerusalem?To what can I compare your calamity,That I may comfort you — O youthful community of Zion?For your rupture is as vast as the sea!Who can possibly heal you?

Forget not how your prophets depicted visions for youThat were false and unsubstantiated.They did not expose your iniquitySo you could repent for your waywardness.Instead they depicted false prophecies for you,And manipulated their messages to cast you off.

It is thus only natural that at first:All passersby clapped their hands at you;They whistled and wagged their headsAt the state of the Jerusalem community:Is this the city that they — our ancestors — would label:The totality of beauty,The joy of all the earth?

It is thus only natural that eventually:All your enemies bared their mouths against you;They whistled and gnashed their teeth,They declared: We have devoured her!Is this not the day we longed for!?At last, we have encountered and seen it!"

YHWH has perpetrated what He purposed.He has carried out His threatJust as He warned in bygone times.He thus shattered without pity.He excited the enemy against you;He exalted the antlers of your foes.

The starving infants cried out their hearts to Adonai!O parents — wall of the Zion community!Let your tears stream down like a creekBy day and by night!Allow yourself no respite,Your eyes no tranquility!

Arise and cry out in the night,As the watchmen’s shifts begin!Pour out your heart like waterBefore the presence of Adonai!Lift your hands to Him;Implore Him for the lives of your children,Who writhe with hungerAt the head of every street.
Look, O YHWH, and beholdTo whom you deliberately delivered this!Should women eat their offspring,Those who they delivered and nurture!?Should priest and prophet be killedIn the "sanctuary of Adonai"?
The young and old are laid on the dirt of the streets;My young women and my young men were felled by the sword.You massacred on the day of your anger;You butchered and showed no pity.
You summoned my enemies from all aroundAs though for a day of festival!On the day of YHWH’s anger,There was neither refugee nor remnant.Those whom I nurtured and reared,My enemy consumed.
POEM III: The Gever’s BalmI am the "gever" of scripture;Who has seen affliction;Dealt by the cane of His — YHWH’s — wrath.
He drove and led meInto complete darkness —Without any light.
He repeatedly rewinds his hand,Turning it against me alone —All day long.
He wore away my flesh and skin;He broke my bones.
He built siegeworks against me;He surrounded me with toxins and tribulations.
He settled me in the depths of darkness,Like those dead for eternity.
He barricaded me so that I cannot escape;He ensured my shackles were heavy.
Even when I scream and plead,He shuts out my entreaty.
He blocked my ways with boulders;He corrupted my paths.
He lies in wait for me like a bear,Like a lion in its lair.
He misdirected my ways.He aggressively pruned me.He made me desolate.
He bent his bow;He positioned me as the target for the arrow.
He plunged into my kidneysThe contents of his quiver.
I became a laughingstock to all my people,The subject of their taunt songs all day long.
He sated me with bitter foods;He quenched me with wormwood.
He ground my teeth on gravel;He pressed my face into the ashes.
My soul was neglected by peace;I was abandoned by good.
And I said:Gone is my endurance;My hopes of YHWH.
The memories of my afflictions and groans,Are like wormwood and toxins.
My soul continually ruminates about them,Becoming stooped within me.
But then I call the following to mind,And become hopeful once more:
That the kindness of YHWH never ceases;That His mercies are never exhausted.
They return anew each morning without fail,O YHWH, how reliable You are.
"YHWH is my portion," says my soul,Therefore I shall place my hope in Him.
YHWH is good to those who yearn for Him,To the soul that seeks Him.
It is good for one to hope and wait patientlyFor the eventual salvation of YHWH.
It is good for the ""To bear a yoke in his youth.
Let him sit alone and wait patientlyLet him accept this yoke upon himself.
Let him put his mouth to the dust,Perhaps there is hope.
Let him offer his cheek to the smiter,Let him be filled with insults.
I agree with your sentiments but this is the reason:For Adonai will not neglect forever.
For after He imposes grief,He offers compassion befitting his abundant kindness.
For He does not afflict out of desire,Nor does He seek to impose grief on humans.
Nor does He seek to crush earthling captives underfoot.
Nor does He pervert the course of justiceWhen man faces up to the Exalted One.
Can one human even miscarry justice against another,Unseen by Adonai?
Who can decree and execute,Without the approval of Adonai?
Do not both evil and goodEmerge from the mouth of the Exalted One?
Thus,How can mortal man complain,When the gever’s ordeals are the consequences of his own sins!?
Let us survey and scrutinise our waysAnd return to YHWH.
Let us arouse our hearts as well as our deedsTo repent to the AlmightyWho seems to have retreated to heaven.
For we transgressed and rebelled,And You did not forgive us.
You shielded yourself with anger,And then you pursued us;You killed,You did not pity.
You shielded yourself with a cloudSo no prayer could pass through.
You made us like mucus and repulsive filthAmong the other peoples.
Thus all our enemies opened their mouths against us.
Thus panic and pitfall became our lot,Devastation and destruction.
From my eye shall descend torrents of water,Over the breaking of my community.
My eye shall flow —It shall not be tranquil;There shall be no respite.
Until YHWH looks down from heavenAnd sees what has befallen us —For it seems that He is currently withdrawn.
Yet, in the interim, my eye and its perspectiveDo more for my soulThan all the penitential wailer women in my city.
For I know my suffering was undeserved:My enemies —Without good reason —Hunted me like a bird.
They flung me alive into a pit;They pelted me with stones.
Rising waters drifted over my head;I said, "I am excised."
I called out to Your name, "YHWH",From the depths of the pit.
I know You heard my voice;Do not obscure your earFrom my request for reprieve,From my plea.
I know You hear my voiceFor You would draw near on the days I called You;You would say, "Do not fear!"
Adonai — You would fight the battles of my soul;You would redeem my life.
YHWH — You have seen the wrong done to me;Judge my cause.
You have seen their vengeful acts,All their plots against me.
YHWH — You have heard their insults,All their plots against me.
How the laughing lips and conversationOf those who rose to challenge meStill deride me all day long.
Behold:Whether they sit or riseI am the object of their taunt songs.
YHWH — Pay them back for their deeds,Inflict them with the same evils their hands perpetrated.
May You hand them heartbreak;May Your curse be upon them!
May You pursue them in anger and annihilate themFrom the earthly realm beneath the heavens of YHWH.
POEM IV: TraumaHow is it conceivableThat the gold has dimmed,That the fine gold’s appearance has changed!?That sacred stones are spatteredAt every street head!?
That the precious children of Zion,Once as grand as gold —Are now evaluated as earthen flasks,The work of a potter’s hands!
That even the jackals proffer the breastAs they nurse their young pups,Yet my community has become selfishly callous;Abandoning their younglike the ostriches in the wilderness.
That the tongue of the suckling babeSticks to its palate for thirst;That the young children beg for bread,But no one provides them.
That those who feasted on delicaciesNow perish in the streets;That those reared in scarlet robesNow embrace the trash heap.
That the sin of my communityHas exceeded the sin of Sodom;For it only suffered momentarily:Overturned in an instant,With no human hand laid on it.
That her princes —Their white hues once purer than snow,Whiter than milk,Their red hues once ruddier than rubies,Their forms once like artisan-cut sapphire —
But now their appearance is blacker than soot;They are unrecognisable in the streets.Their skin has shrivelled on their bodies;Having become as dry as wood.
That the victims of the sword were better offThan the victims of hunger,For once stabbed — their blood drained with haste,And at least they were sated with the produce of the field.
Conversely, among the victims of hunger:The hands of compassionate womenBoiled their own children.They became foodstuff for their mothersAs my community broke down.
That YHWH exploded all His wrath;Pouring out His burning anger.That He kindled a fire in ZionConsuming its very foundations.
The kings of the land,Along with all civilization’s inhabitants,Once thought it impossibleFor oppressor or enemyto enter the gates of Jerusalem.
But now, due to her false prophets’ sins,And her decadent priests’ corruption,Who shed the blood of their righteous challengersIn her midst —
The religiously blind staggered through the streets,Defiling themselves with so much righteous blood,That no one could touch their blood-soaked garments.

"Away! Unclean Ones!", they cried out to the righteous;"Away! Away! Do not touch the sanctum!"They would cry as they fluttered and staggered about;Stating adamantly that the Judeans shall never again live exiled among the nations.

O, how zealously they quashed the true prophecies predicting Jerusalem’s downfall!YHWH has providentially scattered them;He shall no longer behold their plight;For they had no regard for the righteous priests,Nor grace for the scholarly elders.

As long as we remained in Jerusalem,We bought into their false utopian vision:Our eyes looked out for our helpers —Ultimately in vain;We rested our hopes on an allied nation —Ultimately it would not save us.
Thus our enemies closed in,They stalked our movements,They scared us from walking our streets.We sensed that our end was nigh;That our days were numbered,And then — that our end had arrived.
Suddenly,Our pursuers swooped upon us,Swifter than the eagles in the heavens;They chased us on the mountains;They lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
Even our breath of life —The current of our nostrils,The anointed of YHWHFell into their snares —He of whom we said:"In his protective shadowWe shall live alongside the nations".
Rejoice and be gladCommunity of EdomResidents of the land of Uz.For the cup of wrath (Jer. 25:25–27) shall pass your way too;You shall be drunk,You shall be sickened,You shall retch.
Community of Zion:Your corruption is spent,He shall exile you no more.Community of Edom:He has noted your corruption,He has exposed your sin.
POEM V: The PrayerBe mindful, O YHWH, of what has befallen us;Behold and see our disgrace!
Our ancestral lands have been turned over to strangers,Our homes to aliens.
We have become like orphans,With no father on whom to lean;Our mothers have become like widows.
Our own waters we drink for money;Our own wood now comes at a price.
With a yoke on our necksWe are hounded;We are weary,But offered no rest.
Our hands grabbed onto EgyptTo steady our fallOnto AssyriaTo be fed with bread.
Our ancestors sinned but they are no more;We bear the brunt of their corruption.
Those once our slaves are now our rulers;There is no one to deliver us from their hand.
At threat of losing our lives we fetch our bread;Because of the sword lurking in the wilderness.
Our skins are burned as though scorched by an oven;Because of the raging famine.
They raped married women in Zion,Maidens throughout the towns of Judea.
Princes were hung up by their hands;The scholarly elders were shown no respect.
Young men dragged the millstones;The youth collapsed beneath the wooden harness.
-The scholarly elders quit the city gates,--The young men their music —
-Thus the joy of our minds was suspended;--And our dancing was turned to mourning.
Our head’s crown has fallen;Woe to us, for we have sinned!
-Because of this our hearts are sick;--Because of these our eyes have grown dim —
-Because of Mount Zion that is desolate;--Because of the foxes that prowl over it.
Yet You, YHWH, are an eternal presence;Your throne endures from generation to generation.
But why have You forgotten us for what seems like eternity?Why have you forsaken us for so many days?
Restore us to yourself, YHWH,That we may be restored;Renew our days as of old.
For even if You deeply despised us,You unleashed your fury against us to the extreme.
